what_happened: The the person running Athena merged pull request 673 into main by hand. They did not bring main back into the the person running Athena/next5 branch afterwards. The next landing's pull request (675) was built from that branch, so it conflicted with main on CHANGELOG.md, and its checks never ran. The the person running Athena fixed it by recording main as merged into the person running Athena/next5 and the pull request branch with a `-s ours` merge, which left the content unchanged. The the person running Athena then merged 675 by hand once it was green. No job work was judged. This is an the person running Athena intervention, not a rejected job.
cause: Merging a job's pull request is an the person running Athena-run step that goes around Athena's own landing path. Nothing after a hand merge brings the the person running Athena branch back in line with main, and nothing checks that the branch the next pull request is built from contains main's tip. Every landing appends to CHANGELOG.md, so a branch that is behind main conflicts on that file. The next landing then fails before its checks run. The only guard is the the person running Athena remembering to sync the branch.
other_causes: CHANGELOG.md is touched by every landing, so any stale base conflicts on it.
A pull request that conflicts has its checks skipped, so the problem shows up as a missing check run, not as a clear error.
open_hypotheses: The input does not say why 673 was merged by hand instead of with `athena land`, so a gap in the land command or a time-pressure shortcut cannot be ruled in or out.
The input does not say whether Athena has any warning that the the person running Athena branch is behind main.
contradictions: The registry class describes a hand merge that breaks the full history check. Here the visible effect was a CHANGELOG.md conflict, and no history check failure is recorded.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before any landing pull request is opened or merged. It compares the the person running Athena branch with main's tip. If main has moved, for example through a hand merge, the check either merges main into the branch (recording it as merged and keeping content) or refuses with a clear message naming the missing sync. A hand merge of a job pull request would then be caught before the next pull request conflicts.
proposed_request: Add a pre-landing check to Athena. Before `athena land` opens or merges a pull request, it must compare the the person running Athena branch the job was built from with the current tip of main. If main has commits the branch does not contain, such as a pull request merged by hand, the command must either merge main into the branch with a recorded merge that keeps the branch content, or refuse with a message that says the branch is behind main and shows the exact sync command. Acceptance: (1) a test where main gains a commit that edits CHANGELOG.md outside Athena, and a following landing then syncs or refuses cleanly instead of producing a conflicting pull request; (2) a test where the branch is already current, and landing proceeds unchanged; (3) the same check applies when max_concurrency is 1 and when it is above 1; (4) the CHANGELOG.md entry required by the changelog default is added.
